..
KEY MESSAGE 1...

Skies are clearing as expected and should remain mostly clear
overnight.

NW winds will be dropping below 10 mph overnight as a surface 
high builds over the area. As skies clear and winds become light
and variable, expect widespread valley fog to form, lingering 
into early or mid morning hours Tuesday. Overnight lows will be
quite cool, in the upper 40s to mid-50s areawide.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

A much drier air mass settles over the area for Tuesday, with PWATS 
dropping to near 0.50 inches and dew points in the 50s for the 
afternoon. A 1020mb high will remain centered over the area through 
the day, along with upper level ridging as 500mb heights reach 
590dm. After the morning fog burns off and dissipates, expect sunny 
skies, light winds and seasonably warm temperatures in the upper 70s 
to mid-80s. Some modest moisture return begins along the East Coast 
heading into Tuesday night. There could be some stratus clouds 
developing and moving in from the south overnight. Otherwise, expect 
some patchy valley fog development and seasonable lows in the mid 
50s to low 60s.

Moisture begins to gradually increase through the day on Wednesday, 
as the southwest return flow develops on the west side of the 
Bermuda high. PWATs increase gradually up to around 1 inch again by 
late afternoon, and some modest instability could develop as dew 
points recover into the 60s. Expect some scattered cumulus 
development during the day, with a few isolated showers or 
thunderstorms also possible...mainly across NE PA and the Central 
Southern Tier of NY. Overall, much of the area looks to remain dry 
on Wednesday though. It will be warm once again, and a little more 
humid with highs in the low to mid-80s (except upper 80s for the 
Mohawk valley and Syracuse metro area).

KEY MESSAGE 3...

Deep moisture returns to the area Thursday and Friday, with PWATS 
likely hovering around 2 inches. With ample moisture and some 
daytime heating expected, this will create quite a bit of 
instability. 12z GFS is showing 1500-3500 J/kg of MUCAPE over the 
forecast area Thursday afternoon, with 1000-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE at 
the same time. Deep layer shear will be on the lower side, generally 
between 20-30 kts on the western periphery of the strengthening, 
offshore Bermuda high pressure ridge. There does not appear to be 
much of a lifting mechanism, as we are not expecting any strong 
frontal passages on Thursday. It seems minor disturbances and 
shortwaves could ripple through the area from the Ohio Valley and 
western PA. With PWATs progged to be 2 to 2.5 standard deviations 
above normal and surface based CAPE potentially 2000-3000 J/Kg even 
a small trigger could initiate clusters of showers and 
thunderstorms. The ensemble blend (NBM) has 12 hour PoPs of 75-85 
percent on Thursday afternoon, and was inclined to keep this due to 
the above noted setup. Forecast soundings from the NAM and GFS show 
no cap in place Thursday afternoon, with long deep CAPE profiles and 
potentially high DCAPE values. As is typically the case it will 
depend on how much daytime heating occurs. Current model forecast 
push temperatures up into the low to mid-80s for highs.

The setup looks very similar for Friday, but if the 12z GFS is 
correct there would actually be more troughing pushing into the area 
from the west, which would provide more lift. Overall, the exact 
timing and placement of storms remains uncertain during this time 
period...but the setup does look favorable for possible heavy 
rainfall and gusty winds with some the storms. This will be 
something to monitor closely as we get closer in time and specifics 
become more clear. High temperatures remains steady in the low to 
mid 80s on Friday once again.

Moisture and instability remain in place for the upcoming weekend. 
The offshore Bermuda high weakens and retreats eastward. Overall, 
most model guidance keeps a fairly zonal flow over our area Saturday 
and Sunday. Without a strong front or lifting mechanism chances for 
showers or t'storms fade back to isolated or scattered. Temperatures 
remain steady with highs in the 80s and lows in the 60s.
